title: Power chords B B A A G G F# F# B B A A G G E E 140bpm Les Paul
timingNotes: Onsets are pick-attack transients on a three-pole 5kHz-highpassed 1ms RMS envelope, backtracked to 30% of each attack peak above its local floor; the sixteen attacks stand 10-30x above every other peak in that band, so the count is unambiguous. Measured inter-onset intervals are 815-885ms (mean 857.2ms). That is a HALF note at 140bpm (857.1ms), not a quarter: the take is sixteen evenly spaced events, and it contains no quarter/eighth contrast despite the performer's description of "quarter then eighth notes". The 140bpm clock itself is confirmed by the cowboy-chord takes from the same session, whose bars measure 1714ms. Identity comes from FFT peak picking on 8192- and 32768-point windows 100-300ms into each note. Every chord is root+fifth+octave on the low E and A strings; strong partials two octaves and a major third above each root (A#4 over F#2, G#4 over E2, C#5 over A2, B4 over G2, D#5 over B2) are the fifth harmonic of the root, not a major third in the voicing. End times are where each note's RMS falls below 15% of its attack peak: the second note of each pair is muted about 360ms in, leaving a real gap before the next pair. No detector output was used to derive any value here.
